title: Merge k Sorted Lists
statement:
You are given an array of `k` singly linked lists, `lists`. Each list is sorted in non-decreasing order, and any of them may be empty (`null`). Merge them all into **one** sorted linked list and return its head.

Return `null` if there are no nodes at all. You may reuse the existing nodes.
constraints: each list is sorted in non-decreasing order

target.note: O(n log k); the bench uses k = n/8 lists

benchN: total number of nodes (spread over k = n/8 lists)
hints: The next node of the output is always the smallest current head among the k lists. How fast can you find that smallest head, again and again?
Scanning all k heads every step costs O(k) per node. A min-heap of list heads gives you the smallest in O(log k), and after you take a node, only its successor has to go back in.

PriorityQueue<ListNode> ordered by val (use Integer.compare). Offer every non-null head. Poll the smallest, append it to a dummy-headed tail, and offer its next if there is one. Repeat until the heap is empty.
followups: Do it without a heap by merging lists in pairs, like the merge step of merge sort. Why is that also O(n log k), when merging them one after another into a growing result is O(n·k)?
What is the space cost of each approach, and can the pairwise version use O(1) extra space?
How would you merge k sorted files that are each too big to fit in memory?
explain: Keep a min-heap of the current head of each list. Repeatedly poll the smallest, append it to the output (a dummy head avoids the empty-result special case), and push that node's next. The heap never holds more than k nodes, so each of the n nodes costs O(log k): O(n log k) time, O(k) extra space. Divide and conquer gets the same bound with no heap: merge list pairs (0,1), (2,3), … and repeat, giving log k rounds of O(n) work each. The common slow answer merges each list into one growing result, which is O(n·k). In Java, write the comparator as (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a.val, b.val), because a.val - b.val overflows once values approach the int limits.
